teacherGuide.overview: A hide-and-seek rhyme. Form: four couplets. Rhyming pairs: ten/again, before/door, see/tree, you/anew. It teaches counting and safe play.
learningGoals: Name safe and unsafe places to hide.
Take a turn as finder and hider.
beforeReading: Walk the play area and mark the places where hiding is allowed.
afterReading: Play with an adult watching, keeping children away from roads, wells and open water.
discussion: Why must we hide only in safe places?
reflection: Who will you tell if you feel scared while hiding?

support: Hide only in the classroom with an adult.

culturalNotes: Hide and seek is played by children everywhere. The rhyme is original and adds a safety rule: never hide near wells, roads or open water.
localiseThis: Use the safe hiding places in your own school and compound.
